decisions.rationale: Codex's round-1 draft scheduled StoreKit unconditionally (T-010) as a normal milestone with only a services-layer dependency, directly contradicting the explicit go/no-go gate locked three times over in project_plan (attempt only if M1-M5 are done with real time remaining). Since this backlog is meant to be immediately actionable by build workers, including an ungated StoreKit task would guarantee that violation happens.
rejected_alternatives: Including a StoreKit task gated only by a comment/note rather than by simply not existing in the initial backlog
Codex's unconditional StoreKit task
constraints: If StoreKit is attempted later per the existing gate, it gets its own task-assignment pass at that time, reusing the EntitlementGate abstraction already scaffolded in T-016

decisions.decision: Deck management splits into two screens: a Decks list screen (T-021) and a DeckDetailScreen navigation push (T-022) that owns card CRUD, archive/unarchive, permanent delete, and CSV export; R-015 (archive vs. delete as distinct, separately-confirmed actions) belongs to T-022 only, not T-021.
decisions.rationale: Archive/delete/export are actions taken on a specific already-opened deck, not swipe actions off a list row (which the project's own rules forbid routing flows through); modeling them as a detail-screen push is the more honest UI shape and correctly reflects which task actually implements R-015 for the requirement-coverage check to mean anything.
rejected_alternatives: Bundling DeckFormSheet, ArchiveConfirmSheet, and DeleteConfirmSheet all into one 'Decks screen' task (the round-1 draft), which also misattributed R-015 to a task that didn't own the relevant files
Swipe-action or long-press based archive/delete controls
constraints: DeckDetailScreen remains a push destination within the Decks tab, not a fifth top-level screen — the locked four-screen inventory (Decks/Review/Stats/Settings) is unchanged

decisions.decision: CSV import is explicitly excluded from the flows-json UI-crawl gate; its correctness is proven instead by T-019's RecallAppTests (loadPreview/commit against real CSVParseResult fixtures) plus documented manual simulator verification, with the exclusion and its reason recorded in README (T-031).
decisions.rationale: UIDocumentPickerViewController runs as a separate system process outside the app's own accessibility tree, making it an unreliable target for a generic tap/type/assert_exists harness; forcing it into the flow contract would trade real bug-catching value for scripted-picker flakiness.
rejected_alternatives: Attempting to script the system file picker inside a flows-json journey
Silently leaving CSV import untested by any layer
constraints: T-026's acceptance criteria and T-031's README both explicitly document this exclusion so it isn't later flagged as a missed requirement

decisions.decision: DemoDataService.seed() must guarantee at least several cards are due today, not only spread across historical dates, as an explicit T-018 acceptance criterion.
decisions.rationale: The 'enable demo data then immediately review' flow in flows-json depends on cards actually being due right after seeding; a seed that backdates every review into the past with nothing due today would make that flow hit an empty state that has nothing to do with a real defect, silently invalidating a UI-crawl journey.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving seed() timing unconstrained beyond 'realistic 30+ day distribution'
constraints: This is in addition to, not a replacement for, the existing non-degenerate 30+ day distribution requirement on T-018

decisions.decision: Fix the 'Enable demo data and review all decks' flow in the locked flows-json: every grade-button label assertion and every grade-button tap must be preceded by a review.revealArea tap, since grade buttons do not exist on screen until the card is flipped.
decisions.rationale: The flow as locked in task_assignments asserted a grade-button label existed before the reveal tap, and repeated the mistake on the second card after grading advanced the queue — as written it would fail every automated run for a reason unrelated to any real app defect.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping the flow as-is and discovering the failure only when a build worker scripts the XCUITest
Removing the assertion instead of fixing its position
constraints: This corrected flow (only this one changed) supersedes the flows-json locked in task_assignments; all other six flows are unchanged

decisions.decision: T-009's RecallCore adversarial review must be performed by someone/some lane other than whoever authored RecallCore (i.e., not self-certified by data_domain), and its closing artifact must cite specific functions/lines checked against the locked SM2 formula table, DueComputation calendar-day semantics, and CSV adversarial-case list rather than a general sign-off.
decisions.rationale: Three consecutive phases (ios_architecture_review, project_plan, task_assignments) flagged this exact gate as unowned and at risk of becoming a rubber stamp under schedule pressure; naming a concrete non-self-review constraint and a concrete evidence bar closes that risk rather than carrying it into build as an open paragraph.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving T-009's ownership as a generic 'polish_resilience' label with no process constraint
Accepting a general clean-bill-of-health review as sufficient
constraints: T-009 cannot close on a review performed or authored by data_domain
T-009's review artifact must reference specific functions/lines, not general confidence language

decisions.decision: All-decks review scope is confirmed as shipping in the same build pass as single-deck review (T-021/T-023), not deferred to a separate late-sequenced milestone; project_plan's M5-sequenced-last framing is superseded for sequencing purposes only, since the underlying scope-general DueQueryService/SessionEngine were already built in M2.
decisions.rationale: task_assignments' actual 31-task backlog already builds all-decks UI alongside single-deck review with identical dependencies, silently contradicting project_plan's explicit 'M5 attempted only after M3/M4 done' framing; since the expensive engineering work (scope-general query, deck-identity-preserving session engine) was already paid for in M2, merging the UI work is low-risk and should be stated as intentional rather than left as an undocumented contradiction for a build worker to stumble on.
rejected_alternatives: Re-splitting all-decks UI out of T-021/T-023 into a genuinely separate, later-sequenced M5 task to match project_plan literally
Leaving the contradiction undocumented and letting whichever document a build worker reads first win by accident
constraints: StoreKit's M6 explicit go/no-go gate (attempt only if M1-M5 done with time remaining) is unaffected by this and remains as locked in project_plan

decisions.decision: Add an explicit acceptance criterion to T-007: the Card model must include the optional note field (String?, defaulted), consistent with the original prompt's card model and the CloudKit-shape defaulting rule.
decisions.rationale: T-007's acceptance criteria enumerated CloudKit-shape rules, denormalization, and enum/attribute constraints but never explicitly named the note field the prompt requires, which is an omission worth closing before build rather than trusting an implementer to infer it from the original prompt text alone.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving it implicit since the original prompt already specifies it
constraints: This is an additive acceptance-criterion clarification, not a new field or behavior

decisions.decision: The manual QA checklist prioritizes the force-quit mid-session persistence check and the day-boundary/DebugClockOverride check above all other items, explicitly marked as the two highest-value tests in the checklist.
decisions.rationale: build_verification confirmed across every prior phase that this app has never had a real xcodebuild test execution — only a clean build. This means the XCUITests covering these two guarantees have never been confirmed to pass by a compiler; a human running these two checks manually is the first real verification these locked, repeatedly-emphasized promises (force-quit loses nothing, due-ness computed live from one shared source) have ever received.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all six core features as equal-weight checklist items with no explicit prioritization
constraints: A tester following this checklist should run these two items first; if either fails, that is a higher-severity finding than any other checklist item

decisions.decision: CSV import gets full manual adversarial coverage (clean row, quoted-comma row, duplicate, malformed row, non-UTF8 file) as part of this checklist, since it is the only verification surface this feature has beyond CSVImportCoordinator's own unit tests.
decisions.rationale: task_assignments explicitly excluded CSV import from the automated flows.json UI-crawl gate because the system file picker can't be scripted reliably. That means manual QA is not a redundant secondary check for this feature — it's the only place the actual import UI (as opposed to the underlying coordinator logic) ever gets exercised by anything.
rejected_alternatives: Treating CSV import as adequately covered by CSVImportCoordinatorTests.swift alone and giving it a lighter manual pass
constraints: The test CSV file used must include at least one quoted-comma row and one duplicate row, not just malformed/clean rows, to exercise the RFC4180 and duplicate-skip logic specifically

decisions.decision: The checklist includes an explicit negative-check section (§12) requiring the tester to actively look for and confirm the absence of any paywall, subscription, deck-cap, or cloud-sync/marketplace-shaped UI.
decisions.rationale: This build shipped the free-tier StoreKit-deferred fallback per app_features' should-have scoping; a checklist that only tests features present would never catch scope creep (e.g. a stray upsell string or cap check left in from an earlier draft) since absence-of-a-feature isn't naturally exercised by testing the features that do exist.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving paywall/non-goal verification implicit or unstated, relying on the build's own architecture to guarantee absence
constraints: This check must be re-run if StoreKit is ever added in a future phase, at which point this section needs to be rewritten to test the paywall directly rather than its absence

decisions.decision: Recall cannot be declared launch-ready until the human QA checklist's two starred items (force-quit mid-session persistence, day-boundary/DebugClockOverride due-computation) are actually executed by a person on a real simulator, with recorded pass/fail — a clean xcodebuild compile does not satisfy this bar.
decisions.rationale: Every prior phase (build_verification, human_qa_checklist) established that this app has only ever had a confirmed compile, never a confirmed test run; the project's own top priority since prompt_contract has been 'SM-2 provably right, not plausibly right,' so treating a compiled-but-untested app as launch-ready would violate that founding constraint at the last possible moment.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the clean xcodebuild VERIFIED result as sufficient grounds for a launch-ready verdict
Deferring the QA run to post-submission and shipping on the strength of the compile alone
constraints: Launch-readiness verdict is gated on this QA execution; nothing else in this phase's output should be read as overriding that gate

decisions.decision: Lock App Store positioning: name 'Recall — Offline Flashcards,' subtitle 'SM-2 spaced repetition, private,' with description/promotional copy leading with provable local trust (real SM-2 algorithm, nothing leaves the device, true offline-by-design) rather than generic study-app language, and closing with an explicit, honest statement that there is no cloud sync or shared decks by design.
decisions.rationale: The product's locked promise across every phase since initial_discussion has been 'provable local trust,' not flashcard-authoring polish; burying the no-sync fact rather than stating it upfront would read as a bait-and-switch to users switching from Anki/Quizlet, even though the app is free.
rejected_alternatives: Generic study-app marketing language that doesn't foreground the SM-2/offline-trust differentiation
Omitting or burying the no-cloud-sync limitation in the listing copy
constraints: Keyword field may include competitor-adjacent terms (e.g. 'anki alternative') but the visible description should not name-drop competitors directly

decisions.decision: Screenshot plan is six frames captured from a live running simulator with demo data enabled — Decks, Review flip/grade, (optionally) the interval-posting animation, Stats with populated forecast/retention, CSV import preview, and the reminder-toggle Settings screen — not described or mocked.
decisions.rationale: The demo-data toggle exists specifically so first-look screens are never empty; using it for real screenshots is both honest (it's real app-produced content, not fabricated) and the only way to get non-empty, representative screenshots without waiting for organic user history.
rejected_alternatives: Describing screenshot content without actually capturing it from a running build
Using fabricated/mocked screenshot content instead of real demo-seeded app state
constraints: Screenshots cannot be produced until someone launches the app in a simulator and seeds demo data — this is real, sequenced work, not something to mark done by description alone

decisions.decision: App Store Connect's App Privacy section should be filled out as 'Data Not Collected' across every category, with no hedging.
decisions.rationale: PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy already declares zero data collection and there is no network code path anywhere in the app (confirmed architecturally in ios_architecture_review and re-audited in build_verification), so this is one of the few places the project can make a fully accurate, unqualified claim.
rejected_alternatives: Hedging the privacy label with partial-collection categories out of excess caution
constraints: If any future feature introduces even minimal data collection, this label must be revisited alongside the PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest per DEC-ios_architecture_review-009

decisions.decision: Identify and close a previously-undiscussed launch blocker: App Store Connect requires a privacy policy URL and a support URL, neither of which exists anywhere in this project; the fix is a one-page static privacy policy hosted on GitHub Pages (stating no data collection, no accounts, all data on-device) plus a real monitored support email or GitHub Issues link — not new infrastructure, and explicitly not the kind of cloud-sync-shaped gap this project is barred from faking.
decisions.rationale: This is a mandatory Apple submission requirement that nine prior phases never surfaced because none of them were scoped to actual App Store Connect field requirements; unlike cloud sync/marketplace, it requires no ongoing backend and is a trivial one-time static artifact, so it should be built now rather than discovered as a rejection reason later.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving privacy policy/support URL fields blank or deferring them to submission time without a concrete plan
Treating this as an infrastructure gap requiring the same 'honestly document, do not build' treatment as cloud sync
constraints: Both artifacts (privacy policy page, support contact) can be created in parallel with the QA run and do not depend on any code change

decisions.decision: Lock the notification permission explainer copy (title 'Get a daily nudge,' body explaining no numbers you can't trust, a simple nudge, and an explicit 'you can always enable it later from Settings' line) as the pre-permission sheet content; no Info.plist usage-description string is needed since UNUserNotificationCenter doesn't require one.
decisions.rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-004 requires the reminder toggle to never lie about permission state; the 'enable later from Settings' line is the concrete, user-facing expression of the honest re-enable path that architecture decision depends on, so it can't be cut for brevity.
rejected_alternatives: Shorter explainer copy that omits the re-enable-via-Settings guidance
constraints: This copy must ship in the sheet exactly as specified, particularly the re-enable line

decisions.decision: Subscription/paywall review risk is assessed as near-zero since this build ships the free-tier-only fallback with StoreKit deferred; the actual pre-submission task is inverted — grep the shipped UI strings for any leftover 'Pro/Premium/Unlock/Subscribe/Upgrade' remnant or dead paywall-shaped control from an earlier draft, folded explicitly into pre-submission rather than left to the still-unexecuted QA checklist's negative-check section alone.
decisions.rationale: Apple does reject apps for confusing or dead in-app-purchase-adjacent UI; since no paywall was actually built (DEC-app_features-002), the realistic risk is a stray artifact surviving from before that scoping decision, not a paywall compliance failure.
rejected_alternatives: Treating subscription review risk as a standard paywall-compliance review, which doesn't apply since no paywall exists
Relying solely on the QA checklist's negative-check section without an explicit separate grep pass
constraints: This grep check should run as an explicit pre-submission step, not assumed to be covered implicitly by the (still unexecuted) QA checklist

decisions.decision: Age rating clears as 4+ with no ambiguous answers on Apple's questionnaire, since there is no user-generated content shared with others, no web browser, no gambling, and no mature themes anywhere in the app.
decisions.rationale: A straightforward, low-risk determination given the app's fully offline, no-accounts, no-sharing feature set.

decisions.decision: Recall's final status is 'code-complete, unverified' rather than 'done' — the app is not declared launch-ready, and the go/no-go verdict is No-Go for App Store submission pending real execution of the human QA checklist.
decisions.rationale: Every prior phase back through build_verification established that only a clean xcodebuild compile has ever been confirmed; no xcodebuild test run and no human QA execution has ever happened. Declaring the project 'done' at this point would let ten phases of momentum quietly upgrade compiler silence into proof of correctness, directly contradicting this project's own founding priority that SM-2 correctness be provably right, not plausibly right.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the clean xcodebuild VERIFIED result as sufficient for a 'done'/launch-ready verdict
Splitting the difference with a hedged 'mostly ready' verdict that doesn't clearly gate on QA execution
constraints: This No-Go verdict stands until the human QA checklist's two starred items (force-quit persistence, day-boundary due-computation) are actually run by a person with recorded pass/fail
A future phase that reverses this verdict must cite real QA or test-execution evidence, not another hand-trace

decisions.decision: The final review explicitly separates 'code exists and is well-specified' from 'code is confirmed correct,' listing every unverified surface (test suite, both XCUITests, CSV import UI, NotificationScheduler) as named limitations rather than folding them into a generic 'minor gaps' line.
decisions.rationale: This project's own retrospective already flagged a repeated pattern of adversarial review seats being unavailable or rubber-stamping across nearly every phase; a final review that didn't explicitly name this risk would repeat that same pattern at the last possible moment, when the cost of an optimistic misread is highest.
rejected_alternatives: Summarizing verification status as a single generic 'mostly tested, some gaps remain' line
constraints: Any future phase reading this review must treat 'VERIFIED (compiled cleanly)' as a build signal only, never as evidence that tests passed

decisions.decision: Recall's portfolio audit is marked not applicable: this is confirmed as a single-app build (recall-ios-2), with expected app count 1 matching actual app count 1, no sibling folders, no child workflows, and no portfolio-json manifest — consistent with every phase since portfolio_selection.
decisions.rationale: The phase playbook explicitly instructs single-app runs to record non-applicability rather than invent portfolio-shaped work; nothing in ten-plus subsequent phases (design, architecture, build, verification, QA, launch-readiness, final review) ever introduced a second app, companion surface, or collapsed category that would warrant a real audit.
rejected_alternatives: Manufacturing portfolio-shaped findings (e.g. treating the four screens as if they were candidate sibling apps) to give this phase artificial substance
constraints: No portfolio-json manifest should be produced for this project
Any future phase that considers adding a companion surface (widget, Mac app, lite variant) must treat that as new scope requiring its own justification pass, not an extension of this audit

decisions.decision: Backfill note for ticket-tracker import: final_review's four named follow-ups (execute human QA checklist, get a real xcodebuild test run, verify T-009's adversarial review was non-self-certified, create launch artifacts) should become four distinct backlog tickets, and any ticket summarizing build status must carry the 'compiled cleanly, tests never executed' caveat alongside the status, not drop it.
decisions.rationale: Every phase since build_verification has had to actively resist letting 'VERIFIED (xcodebuild)' be misread as 'tests passed'; a lossy Jira/Notion import is exactly the kind of transform that would flatten that nuance into a plain green checkmark.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving backfill format unspecified and trusting whoever imports this to preserve the caveat unprompted
constraints: Any backfilled 'build' status ticket must explicitly state that no xcodebuild test execution has ever occurred in this project's history
